actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 360 - 57 (Roll no. 216). (text: CR H3543)
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 360 - 57 (Roll no. 216). (text: CR H3543)
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H3545)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 1917.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H3543-3544)
Mr. Tiffany moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.

dimensions.assessment: Involves federal agencies, eight Great Lakes states, Indian Tribes, and participants in recreational and commercial fisheries.
dimensions.evidence: States of Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, and Wisconsin and Indian Tribes in those States

dimensions.assessment: Expands an existing fish marking and data collection program to a greater scale through equipment purchases and personnel hiring.
dimensions.evidence: purchase capital and expendable equipment, fish tags, and other items... and hire additional personnel, as necessary

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $2,700,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out the Program $2,700,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a formal statutory program within the Fish and Wildlife Service and mandates interagency collaboration and data sharing.
dimensions.evidence: there is established within the United States Fish and Wildlife Service a program for the mass marking of hatchery-produced fish

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes funding and program activities through a specific five-year window from fiscal years 2026 through 2030.
dimensions.evidence: $2,700,000 for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2030

missing_information: Actual appropriations enacted in future budgets are not specified beyond the authorization limit.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill provides statutory authority and authorizes $2,700,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2030 for the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to conduct fish mass marking operations in the Great Lakes.
